title: When AI-assisted criticism scales, peer review needs an obligation threshold - Nature Machine Intelligence
text:
With assistance from artificial intelligence (AI), a referee can now produce large volumes of manuscript-specific feedback in seconds. Yet determining whether a particular concern changes the paper’s central claim may still require substantial expert attention. AI therefore changes not only how criticism is produced but also its economics: the marginal cost of raising a plausible concern can fall much faster than the cost of evaluating what should follow from that concern. The scarce resource in peer review may consequently shift from generating criticism to judging which criticism matters1,2.In peer review, criticism carries authority. Concerns raised in a referee report rarely remain neutral observations. Authors are typically expected either to address them or to explain why they have not. Traditionally, formulating manuscript-specific concerns required substantial time and attention, which naturally limited how many concerns a referee could raise. AI, however, weakens this constraint.
